chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sanctuary (haram) of the regular well is forty cubits around it. And in another report, fifty cubits, except if it is near a stagnant/decayed spot or by the road, so it becomes less than that, down to twenty-five cubits.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal radius of a well's sanctuary in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the legal boundaries of a well's exclusivity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting communal resources from encroachment. The variation between forty and fifty cubits illustrates the scholarly methodology of reconciling differing reports (ikhtilaf al-riwayat) based on contextual factors like proximity to roads or stagnant water, ensuring equitable access while preserving the owner's rights.
